knowledge:
- key_parameters: tr=A phylogenetic tree object (e.g., of class phylo) ;; td=A matrix or data frame of trait data representing coordinates in the morphospace (typically 2 columns for 2D space) ;; trait=The name of the trait column in the attached data frame to be mapped to the heatmap in geom_tsheatmap ;; resolution=The resolution of the grid for the heatmap in geom_tsheatmap ;; bin=The number of bins used for the heatmap in geom_tsheatmap
- alternatives: phytools=Provides phylomorphospace and phylomorphospace3d functions, but ggtreeSpace is preferred for 2D plots requiring ggplot2-style layer-by-layer annotations and integration with other spatial layers (like maps or histological images)
- when_to_use: Use when you want to visualize evolutionary trajectories of species in a 2D trait space, analyze patterns of convergence/divergence, or overlay additional trait dimensions (like heatmaps) onto a phylomorphospace
- pitfalls: Ensure that the trait data matches the tree tips and nodes correctly; when using geom_tsheatmap, non-finite values outside the scale range may be removed (resulting in warnings from stat_contour_filled)

workflows.name: basic_phylomorphospace
workflows.intent: Create a basic 2D phylomorphospace plot or add it as a graphic layer to a ggplot object
input: trait_data.csv (continuous trait measurements for morphospace coordinates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the phylogenetic tree and trait data ;; 2. Generate the phylomorphospace plot using ggtreespace or add it as a layer using geom_treespace ;; 3. Add tip annotations using geom_tippoint
workflows.code:
tr <- rtree(15)
td <- fastBM(tr, nsim = 2)
ggtreespace(tr, td) +
    geom_tippoint()

tr1 <- rtree(15)
td1 <- fastBM(tr1, nsim = 2)
ggplot() +
    geom_treespace(tr1, td1)

workflows.name: annotated_phylomorphospace_heatmap
workflows.intent: Create an advanced phylomorphospace visualization annotated with a continuous trait heatmap
input: additional_traits.csv (additional trait values for heatmap mapping)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the tree and trait data ;; 2. Initialize the base phylomorphospace plot ;; 3. Attach additional trait data using the %<+% operator ;; 4. Add a heatmap layer using geom_tsheatmap and customize the color scale and theme
workflows.code:
tr <- rtree(15)
td <- fastBM(tr, nsim = 2, bounds = c(0, Inf))
col <- colorRampPalette(c(
    "#FFFFCC", "#FFEDA0", "#FED976", "#FEB24C",
    "#FD8D3C", "#FC4E2A", "#E31A1C", "#B10026"
))(24)
tdex <- data.frame(
    z = fastBM(tr, nsim = 1, bounds = c(0, Inf)),
    node = 1:15
)
p <- ggtreespace(tr, td)
p %<+% tdex +
    geom_tippoint() +
    geom_tsheatmap(
        trait = "z", alpha = 0.7,
        resolution = 0.01, bin = 24
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = col,
        guide = guide_colorsteps(show.limits = TRUE)
    ) +
    theme_treespace2() +
    theme(
        legend.key.height = unit(1, "null"),
        legend.justification.top = "right"
    )
